title: Night Gallery's demands
summary: Sight reading and patterns of macabre scoring.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I broke down all the Night Gallery things that I got because that doesn't measure up to that at all.
But those were what, half hour segments?

One year they were an hour. When I first went to it they were doing hour shows; the second half was half hour segments. Even so, something should be there. One of the things are the performers, because sight reading, if they don't get the message right off the bat, forget it and they were good musicians, but it still sounds like it was being read. It doesn't have that convincing quality.

Would it be difficult like for Night Gallery, the premise of the show was that it was basically the macabre and kind of a horror series, did you find it a problem having to write episdoe after episode basically in that vein?
Yes--a problem, no, but it's something I wouldn't want to do forever.

You find yourself falling into patterns, which is bad, although for me the ability to pick up on a theme and work it through was always a ball, because I never had been in that position before. I enjoyed it in Mickey One too; maybe that's why I like Mickey One.
